purpose: Held-out synthetic evaluation, frozen after v2 prompt authoring and before model inference. Never used to tune v2.

examples.text: The battery on my Ray-Ban Meta dies before lunch. That is frustrating.

labels.rationale: Product battery criticism does not address the traditional brand or assign blame.
evidence_quotes: The battery on my Ray-Ban Meta dies before lunch. That is frustrating.

examples.text: The Ray-Ban Meta camera makes me uncomfortable; my Ray-Ban aviator sunglasses remain excellent.

labels.rationale: Product concern contrasts with retained positive traditional-brand perception.
evidence_quotes: The Ray-Ban Meta camera makes me uncomfortable; my Ray-Ban aviator sunglasses remain excellent.

examples.text: Only Meta is responsible for gathering voice data; Ray-Ban is not at fault.

labels.rationale: The text assigns responsibility solely to Meta and explicitly excludes Ray-Ban.
evidence_quotes: Only Meta is responsible for gathering voice data; Ray-Ban is not at fault.

examples.text: Ray-Ban is at fault for the weak camera indicator on its Meta smart glasses. I blame Ray-Ban, not Meta.

labels.rationale: Responsibility is assigned to Ray-Ban for a product issue, without wider-brand rejection.
evidence_quotes: Ray-Ban is at fault for the weak camera indicator on its Meta smart glasses. I blame Ray-Ban, not Meta.

examples.text: I hold Meta and Ray-Ban equally responsible for the glasses camera secretly recording people.

labels.rationale: Both companies receive explicit accountability, without a stated traditional-brand consequence.
evidence_quotes: I hold Meta and Ray-Ban equally responsible for the glasses camera secretly recording people.

examples.text: What an upgrade. They really earned my trust this time... /s

labels.rationale: Sarcasm suggests dissatisfaction but leaves entities and brand consequences unspecified.
evidence_quotes: What an upgrade. They really earned my trust this time... /s

examples.text: The Wayfarer sunglasses from Ray-Ban look elegant and fit well.

labels.rationale: Traditional eyewear is praised without stated responsibility or a purchase plan.
evidence_quotes: The Wayfarer sunglasses from Ray-Ban look elegant and fit well.

examples.text: Tomorrow I will order Ray-Ban Meta; hands-free navigation looks useful.

labels.rationale: The speaker explicitly plans to buy the useful product.
evidence_quotes: Tomorrow I will order Ray-Ban Meta; hands-free navigation looks useful.

examples.text: I sent my Ray-Ban Meta back because charging kept failing.

labels.rationale: A product return follows a charging defect, without brand-level criticism.
evidence_quotes: I sent my Ray-Ban Meta back because charging kept failing.

examples.text: Because of Meta's surveillance practices, I won't buy Ray-Ban traditional frames anymore.

labels.rationale: Meta surveillance is directly connected to avoidance of traditional Ray-Ban frames.
evidence_quotes: Because of Meta's surveillance practices, I won't buy Ray-Ban traditional frames anymore.

examples.text: Meta's privacy failures made me boycott the wider Ray-Ban brand.

labels.rationale: The speaker causally connects Meta privacy failures to a wider-brand boycott.
evidence_quotes: Meta's privacy failures made me boycott the wider Ray-Ban brand.

examples.text: After the camera controversy, I will never buy traditional Ray-Ban sunglasses again.

labels.rationale: A camera controversy explicitly leads to refusal of traditional eyewear without naming a responsible company.
evidence_quotes: After the camera controversy, I will never buy traditional Ray-Ban sunglasses again.

examples.text: The smart-glasses recording scandal is why I stopped trusting Ray-Ban's entire eyewear brand.

labels.rationale: The text directly links the scandal to whole-brand distrust, without a stated purchase decision.
evidence_quotes: The smart-glasses recording scandal is why I stopped trusting Ray-Ban's entire eyewear brand.

examples.text: Privacy controversies about wearables keep coming up. Ray-Ban's ordinary eyewear has lost its appeal.

labels.rationale: Privacy controversy and reduced traditional-brand appeal co-occur without an explicit causal statement.
evidence_quotes: Privacy controversies about wearables keep coming up. Ray-Ban's ordinary eyewear has lost its appeal.

examples.text: Meta's recording controversies are everywhere. I am also less keen on Ray-Ban as a fashion brand.

labels.rationale: Meta recording controversies co-occur with reduced fashion-brand perception, without a direct causal link.
evidence_quotes: Meta's recording controversies are everywhere. I am also less keen on Ray-Ban as a fashion brand.

examples.text: I distrust Meta's data handling, but I still admire Ray-Ban's classic style and plan to buy another pair.

labels.rationale: Meta distrust contrasts with sustained traditional-brand praise and a purchase plan.
evidence_quotes: I distrust Meta's data handling, but I still admire Ray-Ban's classic style and plan to buy another pair.

examples.text: That news could change my mind, but I haven't decided anything.

labels.rationale: Referent, evaluative direction and purchase decision are not specified.
evidence_quotes: That news could change my mind, but I haven't decided anything.

examples.text: Ray-Ban traditional frames are overpriced. The Meta smart glasses are useful.

labels.rationale: Price criticism of frames is not attributed to a smart-glasses controversy; the product receives praise.
evidence_quotes: Ray-Ban traditional frames are overpriced. The Meta smart glasses are useful.

examples.text: I do not distrust Ray-Ban because of Meta's privacy debate; my core-brand opinion is unchanged.

labels.rationale: Negated distrust and unchanged core-brand perception provide no negative spillover.
evidence_quotes: I do not distrust Ray-Ban because of Meta's privacy debate; my core-brand opinion is unchanged.

examples.text: Because of the smart-glasses camera scandal, I will avoid all Ray-Ban eyewear, not just the Meta model.

labels.rationale: The controversy explicitly motivates avoidance extending from the product to all Ray-Ban eyewear.
evidence_quotes: Because of the smart-glasses camera scandal, I will avoid all Ray-Ban eyewear, not just the Meta model.
